items.title: MCP vs CLI: Benchmarking Tools for Coding Agents
items.content: A data-driven comparison of MCP and CLI approaches for coding agent terminal control
items.contentSnippet: A data-driven comparison of MCP and CLI approaches for coding agent terminal control

summaries.zh:
**MCP与CLI基准测试：编码代理终端控制工具对比**

本文通过数据驱动的方式，对编码代理在终端控制中使用的MCP（模型上下文协议）与CLI（命令行界面）两种方法进行了基准比较。研究聚焦于两者在实际应用中的性能差异与适用场景，为编码代理工具选型提供参考依据。
summaries.en: This article presents a data-driven comparison of two approaches—MCP (Model Context Protocol) and CLI (Command Line Interface)—for enabling coding agents to control terminals. The content focuses on evaluating how these two methods perform in practice, using empirical data to benchmark their effectiveness. However, the article does not provide specific metrics, methodology details, or conclusions beyond establishing the scope of the comparison. The central focus is on determining which approach better supports terminal control in coding agent workflows.

items.title: Prompts are code, .json/.md files are state
items.content: Treating LLMs as shitty general purpose computers we program with natural language. Because throwing shit at the wall wasn't working anymore.
items.contentSnippet: Treating LLMs as shitty general purpose computers we program with natural language. Because throwing shit at the wall wasn't working anymore.

summaries.en: The article argues that prompts should be treated as code and external files (like JSON or Markdown) as state, rather than relying on ad-hoc prompting. It frames LLMs as imperfect, general-purpose computers that are programmed through natural language. This structured approach represents a shift away from trial-and-error methods, which the author suggests are no longer effective. The key idea is to apply software engineering principles—separating instructions from data—to improve control and reliability when working with language models.

items.title: Boxie - an always offline audio player for my 3 year old
items.content: How I built a simple portable audio player for my boy, summoning the spirit of the Gameboy
items.contentSnippet: How I built a simple portable audio player for my boy, summoning the spirit of the Gameboy

summaries.zh: 作者为自己的3岁孩子制作了一款名为Boxie的简易便携式音频播放器。这款设备完全离线运行，设计灵感源自Gameboy掌机，旨在提供简单、专注的听觉体验。文章主要介绍了该播放器的构建思路，强调其朴素实用，适合幼儿使用，避免在线内容干扰。
summaries.en: The article describes creating "Boxie," a simple portable audio player designed for the author's three-year-old son. The device is intentionally always offline, avoiding internet connectivity and distractions. Its design draws inspiration from the classic Gameboy, evoking a nostalgic, child-friendly aesthetic. The project focuses on a straightforward, durable build tailored for a young child's use, providing a dedicated music and audio experience without screens or online features. The summary captures the main purpose: a homemade, offline audio device for a toddler, styled after the iconic handheld console.
